reason: List uninstall in canary --help, and answer uninstall --help (#730): module-size 32936->32960 (+24), measured off 4e3a586. Attributed against the EFFECTIVE ceiling -- the highest matching allowance, fix-async-history-store-all-the-way-up.json (32936, #731) -- not against baselines.json (26965), which check-arch quotes as the left operand of its error and which is the floor rather than the ceiling (#736). So this branch prints 'REGRESSION: 32960 > 26965 (delta 5995)' while its real contribution is 24. Measured empirically, never derived from the printed arrow: origin/main at 3767314 measures 32936 in a fresh worktree with the top allowance temporarily lifted so the verdict prints a currentValue at all -- exactly the figure #731 recorded, so that allowance consumed its ceiling with zero slack and this branch's whole +24 is its own. Attribution split by restoring each source hunk to the branch point one at a time: npm/src/uninstall.ts is +6 and the ts/src pair (cli.ts, cli-commands.ts) is +18; 6 + 18 = 24 and the parts sum to the whole, which is the check that the attribution is real rather than assumed. The same split was measured independently before the rebase (against the older 32792 base, giving 32816) and again after it, and it held at +24 both times -- the branch TOTAL moves with main, the delta does not, which is the thing that made an earlier reading of this number wrong. Test code and markdown contribute ZERO, proven rather than assumed: the pre-rebase base measurement was taken with ts/test/ts-commands-help-conformance.test.ts, npm/scripts/__tests__/uninstall-help.test.js and the CHANGELOG.md entry all still present and only the source hunks reverted, and it returned 32792 -- byte-identical to what an untouched origin/main worktree returns. A later reader should not need to re-derive that. The growth is the fix. The ts/src +18 is the commander stub that makes the command visible (12 lines in cli.ts) plus its handler (6 in cli-commands.ts): `canary uninstall` shipped in 7.0.0 routable and fully functional but absent from `canary --help`, because TS_COMMANDS in npm/src/router.ts and the commander stubs in ts/src/cli.ts are two hand-maintained lists and nothing asserted they agreed. The stub deliberately matches its overlay/doctor siblings exactly -- description, allowUnknownOption, allowExcessArguments, argument, action -- and was NOT shrunk to save lines: #730 is a bug precisely because two hand-maintained lists drifted, so a stub that deviates from its siblings to buy back 18 lines would re-create the class this PR exists to close, and a fourth TS-handled command should be able to copy one shape rather than choose between three. The npm/src +6 is the smaller half of the same report: the router dispatches uninstall BEFORE the engine's commander sees the argv, so `canary uninstall --help` reached the handler as a plain token and was rejected as 'unknown option "--help"' -- telling a user who asked how the command works that they had used it wrong. Note this is why the issue's own suggested fix is incomplete: no engine-side stub can reach that path. It is only +6 because the scope menu was extracted to one SCOPE_HELP constant shared by the new --help path and the pre-existing no-scope refusal, which deleted a duplicated copy of the menu; the first draft wrote a second usage string and cost +19. Splitting further would not help -- module-size is a repo-wide aggregate, so N files summing to 24 score identically to one, and per #711's recorded finding a new module scores WORSE because it adds its own header and imports. Nothing was absorbed here to avoid a fix: newViolations is 0 and totalViolations is 20, identical to origin/main measured in the same worktree, and no threshold, ceiling, or baseline was raised -- baselines.json is untouched. Entropy is 267 on this branch and 267 on origin/main, a delta of zero, because the one new export (uninstallCmd) has a real caller in ts/src/cli.ts. The durable half of the change costs the metric nothing, being test code: ts/test/ts-commands-help-conformance.test.ts reads TS_COMMANDS from its declaration in router.ts -- not a hardcoded copy, which would be a third list with the same drift problem -- and asserts every entry appears in the engine's help, failing loudly on a zero-length parse rather than passing vacuously. It was mutation-checked: with the stub removed it fails on uninstall while overlay and doctor still pass.
